best_human.provenance: Frozen Colbourn table reports a 39-row Hadamard (Colbourn-Keri) construction with NCK postoptimization.

best_public.provenance: Colbourn November 2024 snapshot. The archive entry records the construction family and row count.
best_public.evidence_state: public upper bound; witness not independently reproduced
best_public.origin_type: human construction as attributed by the archive

best_reproduced.provenance: NIST IPOG-F array. Each dash in the published file was set to zero; the completed array passes exact coverage checking.
best_reproduced.ai_provenance: No AI provenance stated by NIST.
best_reproduced.evidence_state: Exact witness independently replayed and accepted by Sol on 2026-11-06.

search_metadata.algorithm: 256 seeded random rows, exact uncovered-pattern repair, then seeded greedy row deletion
search_metadata.replay: MATHBENCH_SEED=7; call tasks/t023/baseline.py run_code() then tasks/t023/check.py validate()

bounds.lower_bound_reason: Column deletion reduces any 20-column candidate to a 13-column strength-four CA, whose optimum is proved to be 32.
bounds.status: open interval; CAN(4,20,2) not claimed solved

survey_scope_note: Checked the NIST CA(4,k,2) library, the frozen November 2024 Colbourn table, arXiv:1711.10040, and exact-parameter web searches on 2026-11-06. This is not a complete literature survey.
frozen_human_baseline_type: NIST IPOG-F array replay; weaker than the best reported public construction

admission_source_review.human_baseline: Sol independently reproduced NIST IPOG-F 65 rows after completing dash entries as zero.
admission_source_review.reported_record: Sol read the Colbourn mirror row: t=4,v=2,k=20,N=39, Hadamard (Colbourn-Keri) postop NCK. The 39-row witness is not reproduced.
admission_source_review.optimality: CAN(4,13,2)=32 proved in arXiv1711.10040v2 implies lower bound 32 by column deletion. No proof of optimality for 20 columns was found in the checked sources.
admission_source_review.independent_quantity: 4845 column subsets and all 16 patterns in each subset checked separately from the bit-mask checker.
